# Parent Guide attribution simplification — approved local decision

19 November 2026. The owner explicitly answered **“Approve the local simplification”** to the concrete proposal below. It is now implemented locally, separately from the previously approved removal of the marketing checkbox. This decision does not approve publication or provider/account changes.

**Subsequent owner decision:** the entire guide form and Web3Forms integration are now removed in favour of a direct PDF download. This supersedes the required name/email/tier and provider-contract preservation bullets below, which record the earlier approved step. The analytics-only choice and no-migration policy remain current. Historical records are untouched. See the [current release-readiness report](human-hull-release-readiness.md).

## Approved change, implemented locally

- Remove the guide's three hidden `UTM Source`, `UTM Medium` and `UTM Campaign` fields and their population/submission handler.
- Remove the separate Guide campaign attribution choice. Keep a single, initially off Website analytics checkbox, equally prominent reject/save actions, withdrawal and the existing accessible dialog.
- Use the analytics-only `hmt_analytics_v3` session preference with `allow`/`reject` values. Treat every obsolete v1/v2 choice, including `campaign`, `both` and `analytics`, as insufficient for this new version. Only a fresh affirmative analytics choice can enable GA4. There is no transfer from campaign consent to analytics consent. Missing/unknown preferences keep analytics off and clear writable known GA cookies.
- Keep the existing GA measurement ID and event names. Preserve URL/referrer redaction and the current seven analytics-enabled pages. Do not add analytics to the guide or download page, invent download events or weaken redaction to obtain campaign reports.
- Preserve the guide's required first name/email/tier, public provider key, native action, spam field, resource/subject fields, production redirect and PDF. Existing notification records and historical consent evidence are untouched.

## Business implications

Future guide notifications will no longer identify which source/medium/campaign produced an individual request. Any provider integration expecting those optional fields needs owner review. Existing analytics on tuition pages can continue after opt-in, but the guide/download pages currently have no GA configuration and query strings are redacted. Exact guide-request or campaign reporting is therefore not promised. Introducing it would require a separately reviewed measurement change.

There is no irreversible provider/data operation in this change. No historical submission, marketing-consent record, account setting or mailing list is deleted or changed. Obsolete cookies are ignored rather than promoted into new permission. The local source change itself is reversible. No launch or publication is authorised.

**Status: owner-approved and implemented locally.** There is now only one optional measurement purpose. Rejection also sends the existing compatible stop message to already-open v2/v3 tabs; a previously loaded old page otherwise needs a refresh to receive the new code. No claim is made that a new script can remotely rewrite an already-loaded document. Current verification and remaining privacy/provider decisions are recorded in the [release-readiness report](human-hull-release-readiness.md).

# Human / Hull final pre-launch audit

> **Historical audit snapshot.** The subsequent owner confirmation covers commercial use of both new photographs, without enabling either publication flag. The original evidence and findings below are preserved as the audit baseline, not presented as current unresolved statuses.

Audit date: 19 November 2026. Branch: `feature/human-hull-redesign`.

## 1. Executive summary

**Verdict: NO-GO for public release today.** The redesigned pages render correctly once loaded, preserve their established metadata and routes, and pass the tested local enquiry and guide form contracts. Release still needs separate photographic permissions, an approved privacy/analytics treatment, resolution of reproducible mobile cold-load movement, and genuine provider/browser checks on an authorised preview.

This is an independent inspection of the current working tree, not reliance on earlier review notes. No implementation was changed. This report is the only repository file created during this audit. No commit, push, merge, deployment, permission approval or real test enquiry was performed.

The principal evidence is:

- Local `main`, recorded `origin/main`, the remote `main` SHA returned by `git ls-remote`, and the current Netlify production deployment all agree on `be72d0bf8d535aee5fb2e60d2b4ff41fc32cc444`.

- Mocked Netlify success, HTTP failure, network failure, duplicate prevention, status feedback and the thank-you route pass. Native forms also submit correctly with JavaScript disabled. The guide's consent fields, UTM fields, redirect field and PDF pass local contract tests. Provider delivery and notifications remain unverified.
- Mobile Lighthouse cold-load CLS was **0.253 on the homepage** and **0.126 on About and the guide** in the final isolated runs. Delaying navigation initialisation independently reproduces the header collapse. Settled screenshots do not reveal this defect.

## 3. Tests independently performed

| Test | Result and scope |
| --- | --- |
| Repository integrity | Branch, working tree, full tracked diff, all untracked file groups, remote baseline SHA and production deploy metadata inspected |

Browser: headless Chromium 149 on Windows, Playwright. External requests were blocked for functional/layout tests. One initial HTTP sweep hit `ERR_NO_BUFFER_SPACE`; the completed 80-case sweep used direct interception serving the exact exported bytes. Consequently that sweep verifies rendering, not production CDN behaviour. Separate GET checks verified production resources, and Lighthouse used a real loopback HTTP server on port 8768.

HTML validation finds no new rule categories/counts relative to the corresponding baseline pages. Existing findings include raw ampersands, nonbreaking telephone spacing, whitespace and legacy void/doctype style. No parse-breaking markup was found. Guide honeypot attribute warnings are not evidence of failed provider protection.

Detailed machine-readable results, temporary scripts, fresh screenshots and Lighthouse JSON files are in `%TEMP%\human-hull-final-audit\`. They are not public output or release dependencies.

## 4. Critical findings

No verified critical software/security vulnerability, broken enquiry submission contract or site-wide indexing failure was found in this audit. This is not a penetration-test guarantee. The high-priority release gates below still prevent a public GO decision.

## 5. High-priority findings

### H1 — Photographic publication permissions remain outstanding

- **Severity/type:** High; unresolved business permission and mandatory release prerequisite.
- **Evidence/location:** `scripts/prepare-public.mjs:12` independently guards the homepage photograph; line 19 independently guards the About photograph. `index.html:35` and `about-amir/index.html:59` identify local-testing use. No permission clearance was supplied. The latest brief states the outdoor portrait was originally taken by a friend and subsequently lightly AI-adjusted; local cropping/compression does not resolve ownership or derivative-use rights.
- **Impact:** The approved photographs cannot yet be safely published. The normal public build intentionally fails while approvals are unset.
- **Recommended resolution:** Obtain separate written permission/provenance for the professional school photograph and the friend-taken outdoor portrait, including intended commercial website use and supplied edits. Also resolve the legacy social-preview image provenance described in section 13. Only then should an authorised release operator approve the corresponding flags. Keep both guards intact.
- **Launch blocker:** **Yes.** This is not a request to bypass a build failure.

### H2 — No documented privacy/analytics controls in the website

- **Severity/type:** High; verified implementation/information gap, with a business/legal determination still required. Pre-existing, not introduced by the redesign.
- **Evidence/location:** `script.js:1–13` configures and loads GA immediately. No consent default/gate, objection mechanism or privacy-policy page/link is present in the export. The enquiry at `index.html:93` collects contact details; the guide at `year-11-parent-guide/index.html:113` sends details to Web3Forms. Its short note at line 148 explains marketing choice but is not a complete processing notice.
- **Impact:** Visitors lack clear information and usable controls covering analytics and enquiry/guide processing. This audit cannot clear the privacy position or unseen GA account settings.
- **Recommended resolution:** Have the owner approve an accurate notice covering purposes, providers, retention, rights and contact details, and choose/document an appropriate analytics control model. Do not assume analytics always require a banner or that all analytics are exempt: current [ICO storage/access guidance](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guidance-on-the-use-of-storage-and-access-technologies/what-are-the-exceptions/) makes the statistical exception conditional, including information and an easy objection route. The tested implementation supplies neither those controls nor a consent mechanism. Account configuration and final legal applicability need review before an approved fix.
- **Launch blocker:** **Yes, pending owner privacy review and an approved remedy.** No tracking or form implementation was changed during this audit.

### H3 — Mobile navigation initialisation causes visible cold-load movement

- **Severity/type:** High; verified visual-stability defect in the shared redesigned header.
- **Evidence/location:** `navigation.js:16–17` reveals the toggle and adds `home-nav-ready` after load; `styles.css:3085–3089` displays the navigation before that class and hides it afterwards. Final isolated mobile Lighthouse CLS: homepage **0.253**, About **0.126**, guide **0.126**. A separate 600ms navigation-script delay moves the top of `main` from about **249px to 77px**. Font swaps add further homepage movement (`styles.css:1–14`).
- **Impact:** Content jumps during loading on slower mobile connections. A user can lose reading position or a tap target. Settled approval screenshots remain correct but do not cover this state.
- **Recommended fix:** Initialise the enhanced navigation state before first paint, while preserving the working no-JavaScript navigation; avoid a height-changing header transition. Review font preload/fallback metrics to reduce the separately measured font movement. Retest cold mobile loads and retain the existing design.
- **Launch blocker:** **Recommended technical release blocker.** Resolve and remeasure before presenting the mobile release as stable. These are local lab results, not field Core Web Vitals.

## 6. Medium-priority findings

### M1 — Legacy download header overflows with enlarged text

- **Severity/type:** Medium; verified accessibility/resizing defect, pre-existing.
- **Evidence/location:** `year-11-parent-guide/download/index.html:24–28` retains the legacy header, unlike the guide page. At 768px with root text enlarged to 200%, document width becomes **927px**, and brand/navigation extend beyond the viewport. Screenshot: `%TEMP%\human-hull-final-audit\download-text-200.png`.
- **Impact:** Readers using larger text need horizontal scrolling on a lead-conversion destination. Default-size scans miss this.
- **Recommended fix:** Apply a compatible wrapping/navigation treatment to that utility header, scoped to avoid altering approved pages. Retest actual browser text/zoom controls and keyboard access. Its native skip link already works: the next Tab after activation reaches “Download the PDF”.
- **Launch blocker:** Not a site-wide release blocker by itself; a known defect that should be resolved before claiming complete resizing accessibility.

### M2 — Secondary-page A-Level navigation loses the service context

- **Severity/type:** Medium; verified conversion/usability defect in the new navigation.
- **Evidence/location:** Secondary headers, for example `about-amir/index.html:53`, link to `/#enquire` with `data-enquiry-service="A-Level Maths"`. `navigation.js:72–75` can update only a form in the current document. Tested About → A-Level navigation lands on the homepage with **GCSE Maths** selected. The homepage's own A-Level CTA correctly selects A-Level.
- **Impact:** A-Level enquiries can arrive miscategorised unless the visitor notices and changes the selection. The message still submits; the route is not broken.
- **Recommended fix:** Carry the intended service through navigation using a validated state/query/fragment contract, then apply it on the homepage. Preserve the form name, field values and established route. Generic Maths MOT → homepage enquiry links also default to GCSE; consider their service context in the same approved fix.
- **Launch blocker:** No; fix is recommended before release to improve lead accuracy.

### M3 — Schema business and website references have no definitions

- **Severity/type:** Medium; verified structured-data completeness defect, pre-existing.
- **Evidence/location:** Seven secondary documents reference `https://hullmathstutor.co.uk/#business`; the guide also references `/#website` (`year-11-parent-guide/index.html:33–34`). Neither ID is defined in any public JSON-LD graph. The homepage has no JSON-LD, including at baseline. Example provider reference: `about-amir/index.html:31`.
- **Impact:** Machines receive incomplete entity relationships. This does not invalidate canonical URLs or prevent indexing.
- **Recommended fix:** Add approved, factually accurate business/site entity definitions using the already referenced IDs, or deliberately revise the references after SEO approval. Do not invent address, opening hours, ratings or credentials.
- **Launch blocker:** No. No established metadata change is required to address it.

## 7. Low-priority findings

### L1 — Shared CSS contains substantial unused rules per page

- **Severity/type:** Low; optional performance/maintenance improvement.

# Human / Hull release-blocker remediation

> **Historical first remediation pass.** The owner has since confirmed commercial-use permission for both new photographs; M1/M2 are now fixed and privacy choices are granular. See the [current release-readiness report](human-hull-release-readiness.md) for current status, remaining privacy decisions and the independent legacy learner-image issue. Earlier outstanding-status statements below describe this pass's original state. Publication flags remain disabled by the workflow.

19 November 2026. Local work on `feature/human-hull-redesign`, following a full reading of `human-hull-final-audit.md`.

**Technical consent controls and the reproduced cold-load defect are resolved in local testing. Public release remains NO-GO:** photographic permissions, owner-confirmed privacy information and authorised live release checks are still outstanding. The privacy notice is explicitly a local review draft, not a representation that unknown legal/business facts have been verified.

No commit, push, merge, deployment, real enquiry or external analytics collection event was performed. Neither photograph was published or cleared. No new dependency, framework or unrelated design change was introduced.

## 1. Findings resolved

### H2: default-off optional measurement and accessible controls

The old unconditional Google loader in `script.js` has been replaced by the consent-gated `privacy.js` service. The measurement ID remains **G-FTB362ESXH**. Existing event names remain `generate_lead`, `phone_click`, `whatsapp_click` and `maths_mot_click`.

The chosen implementation is explicit opt-in consent, with Google's **basic** loading model: no Google tag, measurement queue, consent-status ping or analytics event before acceptance. Merely loading a tag with denied consent can still produce cookieless measurements in advanced mode; that model is not used. See [Google's basic/advanced explanation](https://developers.google.com/tag-platform/security/concepts/consent-mode).

Footer links provide the privacy notice and Analytics settings on every content/confirmation page. The settings link works as a notice-section link without JavaScript and becomes an accessible dialog control when enhanced. There is no automatic overlay interrupting the approved pages. Until a visitor actively chooses Allow analytics, optional measurement stays off.

The dialog gives equally styled Allow/Reject choices, no preselected option, initial heading focus, native modal keyboard containment, Escape handling and focus return. It explains both Google Analytics and consent-gated guide campaign attribution. Refusal does not prevent enquiries, downloads or normal browsing. This follows the [ICO's current consent-mechanism guidance](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guidance-on-the-use-of-storage-and-access-technologies/how-do-we-manage-consent-in-practice/?search=iss).

Implementation details:

- A first-party **session** cookie, `hmt_analytics_v1`, remembers only allow/reject; it does not contain a visitor identifier. Browser session restoration can affect its lifetime. No fixed business-record retention period has been invented.
- Google identifier cookies are requested as session cookies using `cookie_expires: 0`, verified against a locally executed copy of the real tag. This does **not** establish Google's server-side retention. [Google documents that cookie setting separately](https://developers.google.com/tag-platform/security/guides/customize-cookies).
- Advertising storage, advertising user data and advertising personalisation default to denied. Google signals/ad-personalisation signals are disabled, advertising data redaction is enabled and URL passthrough is disabled.
- Configured page URLs omit query strings/fragments; configured referrers use the origin only. The app event API accepts only the existing event names and their existing non-personal parameter keys. It does not queue declined interactions for later replay.
- Withdrawal sets Google's documented disable flag, clears this site's two known GA cookies, synchronises other open tabs and leaves unfinished form text intact. It does not reload the page. [Google documents the opt-out flag](https://developers.google.com/tag-platform/security/guides/privacy).
- Already collected/queued consented hits can finish after a choice change; withdrawal cannot recall in-flight data or erase provider records. Tests separately establish that new collection is suppressed after withdrawal, including withdrawal before the tag download finishes.
- If saving the preference is blocked, analytics remains off and an accessible status message explains why. If the privacy script fails completely, `script.js` still handles enquiries and has no independent Google loader.

### Actual data flows and PECR treatment

The [ICO's final storage/access guidance](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guidance-on-the-use-of-storage-and-access-technologies/?search=iss), finalised 29 April 2026, was checked during this work. Its [statistical-purpose exception](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guidance-on-the-use-of-storage-and-access-technologies/what-are-the-exceptions/) is narrow: aggregate service-improvement statistics, restricted individual-level processing, appropriate provider roles/use restrictions, information and a free objection mechanism. It is not a blanket exemption for installing GA4.

This site's existing visitor identifiers and linked event histories, and the guide's person-linked campaign attribution, do not establish those conditions. No evidence of an aggregate-only provider/retention arrangement was available. **No statistical-purpose exception is relied on for either optional measurement flow.** Both require an affirmative analytics choice in this implementation. The essential preference cookie is used solely to remember that requested privacy choice, not as an analytics identifier.

| Flow verified from source and tests | Handling after remediation | Still unverified |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Page/resource requests to Netlify, including ordinary network metadata | Normal hosting continues independently of analytics choice; fonts remain self-hosted | Hosting log retention and contractual/transfer details |
| GA4 on the seven existing analytics-enabled pages | Tag and events blocked until acceptance; existing names/ID preserved | Account retention, enhanced measurement/data sharing/link settings, processor and transfer arrangements |
| Netlify enquiry: name, email, optional phone, service, message and honeypot | Same fields, validation, URL-encoded AJAX POST to `/`, native POST to `/thank-you/`, statuses and success redirect | Actual notification recipients, inbox retention, live delivery and processor arrangements |
| Web3Forms guide: first name, email, tier, resource details, optional marketing choice | Native provider submission, spam field, existing key and production download redirect preserved | Provider recipients/account controls, notification delivery, retention and transfers |
| Guide UTM source/medium/campaign | Same hidden field names; populated only after analytics consent, blank when declined/no JS, cleared on withdrawal and rechecked at submission | Owner's use/retention of attributable guide records |
| Optional email-updates checkbox | Still unchecked by default; choice recorded independently of analytics | Whether/how emails are sent, mailing provider, suppression/deletion process |
| Email, phone and WhatsApp links | Activated only when the visitor chooses a link; no new embedded tracker | Off-site service/account practices |

The previous guide code read campaign parameters unconditionally and attached them to the requester. That is optional measurement rather than necessary PDF delivery. The [ICO explicitly includes link decoration and navigational tracking](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guidance-on-the-use-of-storage-and-access-technologies/what-are-storage-and-access-technologies/?search=iss); storing campaign attribution alongside contact details cannot simply be described as anonymous aggregate statistics. The old inline population code is now handled by the same explicit choice. Form/provider contracts remain intact; campaign values are intentionally absent without consent.

No local storage or session storage is introduced. Browser caching of public files and ordinary requested form delivery are separate from optional analytics. Forms do not require an analytics choice or an extra privacy-agreement checkbox. Their appropriate UK GDPR lawful bases and the business's record handling still require owner confirmation.

### H3: cold-load layout stability

The mobile navigation's initial layout is now established by a tiny inline head marker before CSS paints. The main navigation script remains **deferred**. CSS uses that early state, rather than waiting for the later header class to change height. Without JavaScript the full navigation is available; a failed navigation-script request removes the enhancement marker and exposes the links.

Both existing WOFF2 fonts are preloaded. Measured local Arial/Georgia fallback faces use size/vertical-metric adjustments while those fonts arrive. The fallback faces are restricted to Latin text/punctuation so unsupported arrow glyphs retain their original fallback appearance. Primary Inter/Playfair choices, sizes, weights, image dimensions, portrait crop/corners and settled content layouts remain unchanged.

No loading screen, artificial implementation delay, new height animation, blanket transition suppression or hidden-until-loaded page was introduced. A delayed-navigation test confirms content still paints before that deferred script arrives.

## 2. Files changed

Changed existing implementation files, relative to the start of this remediation:

| File(s) | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `script.js` | Remove unconditional Google startup; route existing events through the consent gate. Form-handling logic unchanged |
| `navigation.js` | Work with the early layout marker and retain deferred initialisation, menu/focus and link behaviour |
| `styles.css` | Font fallback metrics and early navigation selectors only |
| `index.html` | Font hints, early marker/deferred navigation, privacy loader, footer links and short enquiry processing notice |
| `about-amir/index.html` | Shared head loading hints/marker and privacy footer/loader |
| `gcse-maths-tutor-hull/index.html` | Same shared integration |
| `gcse-maths-tutor-prices/index.html` | Same shared integration |
| `gcse-grade-4-5-maths-support-hull/index.html` | Same shared integration; established URL retained |
| `functional-skills-maths-tutor-hull/index.html` | Same shared integration |
| `maths-mot-hull/index.html` | Same shared integration |
| `year-11-parent-guide/index.html` | Shared integration, linked processing notice, consent-gated attribution replaces unconditional inline population |
| `year-11-parent-guide/download/index.html` | Font hints and privacy footer/loader; no GA or route changes |
| `thank-you/index.html` | Font hints and privacy footer/loader; no GA or form-result changes |
| `scripts/prepare-public.mjs` | Allowlist the three new privacy assets/page; both photograph guards unchanged |

New implementation files: `privacy.js`, `privacy.css`, `privacy/index.html`. The new notice is related to the blocker, uses the existing system, is clearly marked as a draft, and is `noindex,follow` rather than added to the sitemap.

Review artifacts: this report and [mobile settings](visual-review/release-blockers/privacy-settings-390.png) / [desktop settings](visual-review/release-blockers/privacy-settings-1440.png) screenshots. Existing reference/review files and all photograph/image assets are unchanged.

## 3. Before-and-after measurements

Fresh matched tests compare a saved pre-remediation source snapshot with the implementation. Chromium 149 on Windows; loopback HTTP; cache disabled; 150ms latency, 1.6384Mbps download, 675Kbps upload and 4× CPU slowdown at **all** listed widths, including desktop. Analytics unconsented; external requests blocked. Each case has three cold runs. Observe through font readiness plus one second; compute the maximum layout-shift session window (one-second gap/five-second limit), excluding recent-input shifts.

| Case | Before median CLS | After median CLS |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Homepage 320px | 0.197195 | 0.000000 |
| Homepage 375px | 0.271763 | 0.000000 |
| Homepage 390px | 0.314429 | 0.000000 |
| Homepage 1440px | 0.000777 | 0.000000 |
| About Amir 390px | 0.122059 | 0.000000 |
| Parent guide 390px | 0.139760 | 0.000000 |

All three observed runs matched within each case: **18 before and 18 final after runs**. These are reproduced measurements under a controlled CDP profile, not a comparison of unlike Lighthouse scores or real-user Core Web Vitals. No INP or field performance claim is made.

Additional targeted single-run stress tests, on otherwise unthrottled loopback at 390px:

| Artificial resource delay used only in the test | Before CLS | After CLS |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| WOFF2 responses delayed 1200ms | 0.198837 | 0.000539 |

# Retention and deletion - monthly operating procedure

20 November 2026. Operator: Amir Hedjazi, sole trader trading as Hull Maths Tutor. **Owner-approved on 20 November 2026, alongside the Privacy & Cookies Policy.** No reminder has been created and no customer record has been inspected or deleted by this task. New Parent Guide downloads create no form records; the guide procedure concerns historical requests only.

## Dates and exceptions

| Record | Limit for copies controlled by the business | Calculate from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unsuccessful tuition enquiry, notifications and related correspondence | 12 calendar months | Original receipt; use the last day of the month if the anniversary date does not exist |
| Historical Parent Guide request with no continuing purpose | 90 calendar days | Original request, not a later email, export or internal note |
| Active tuition records | While needed to provide/administer tuition | Keep only relevant information; review when tuition ends |
| Necessary accounting/tax, complaint, rights-request or legal-claim records | Applicable legal period or justified continuing need | Record purpose, applicable obligation where relevant, limited scope and next review date |

A genuine new enquiry has its own date. Do not restart old records' clocks by exporting, forwarding or making notes. Delete sooner when no longer needed. Do not classify every old guide/enquiry email as an active student record. Historical consent evidence, if needed to show a past choice, is a scoped exception with its own reason and review date; it does not permit new marketing. This is not a new indefinite archive.

## One monthly appointment

Owner action: put a recurring reminder on the **first working day of each month**, with the first review before public launch. Check records already due and those due **before the next appointment**, deleting unnecessary copies early so a monthly review does not routinely add a month. If an exception genuinely must last until a precise date, set a separate reminder. Record and remedy missed reviews promptly.

1. Identify active tuition, financial records and justified holds first. Work only on eligible records; do not delete a form, account or whole financial archive.
2. **Netlify:** in Forms > enquiry, select and delete only eligible individual submissions, checking relevant Spam entries too. Preserve the `enquiry` form. [Official submission controls](https://docs.netlify.com/manage/forms/submissions/). A deploy-artifact expiry is not form retention.
3. **Gmail:** remove matching notifications, replies and unnecessary attachments from the configured Gmail Inbox/All Mail, Sent and accessible Trash, checking any synced local mail copies. The owner confirms direct replies from this inbox and no knowingly configured forwarding/external enquiry manager; do not invent extra destinations. Archiving alone is not deletion. Gmail normally keeps Trash for 30 days; use permanent deletion for eligible messages in the review. [Gmail deletion instructions](https://support.google.com/mail/answer/7401?hl=en).
4. **Historical Web3Forms:** once, establish whether historical records still exist and whether the account offers individual deletion; if they do, use that control or request deletion through the provider's published privacy/support contact. Specify only the necessary record identifiers privately. Do not export an entire history just to identify a few records. Record requests as pending until confirmed, and follow up at the next review. Do not claim that Gmail deletion purges Web3Forms. Its [privacy policy](https://web3forms.com/privacy) and [DPA](https://web3forms.com/dpa) do not provide an automatic 90-day account purge. Historical account contents/plan and earlier deletion have not been inspected here. If there are no records in that location, record that and stop checking the retired integration unnecessarily.
5. **Exports/copies:** check known Downloads, local/cloud files, spreadsheets, attachments, accessible recycle bins and version histories; remove eligible copies/rows. Do not create new bulk copies to perform deletion. Keep any necessary export private, out of Git/the website, with the original due date.
6. Make the short private log below; note outstanding provider actions and scoped exceptions. Verify completion of a requested action before marking it complete. Keep no names or message bodies in this housekeeping log; review the log's own continuing need at each review.

## Provider copies and limits

Netlify's [DPA](https://www.netlify.com/pdf/netlify-dpa.pdf/) distinguishes termination deletion from backup/log rotation; it does not specify a fixed live-form expiry. Do not cancel the account to meet this procedure. Web3Forms' DPA distinguishes submission lifetime, termination and residual backups; ask about the particular historical records, not an invented automatic purge. Account visibility is not proof of physical erasure.

Google's [deletion explanation](https://policies.google.com/technologies/retention?hl=en-GB) describes an approximately two-month process and backups up to six months, with exceptions/delays. These are provider limits, not something this monthly procedure can accelerate or certify. Netlify has not published a universal backup rotation duration in the DPA reviewed. Ask the provider only if a specific outstanding request needs a recovery-copy answer; an unknown universal number does not prevent an accurate notice based on retention criteria. If restoring a business backup, reapply recorded deletion decisions before returning obsolete records to routine use.

The owner-confirmed GA4 two-month event/user retention, reset off, is separate from these business records and session cookies. No account change or historical deletion has been performed here.

Handle access, correction, erasure, objection and withdrawal requests when received, without waiting for the monthly review. Verify identity proportionately, find the relevant copies/holds and respond within applicable deadlines. Analytics withdrawal stops new optional collection; it cannot recall in-flight requests or automatically erase provider history.

## Minimal private log - outside Git

```text
Review date / operator / next appointment / look-ahead cutoff:
Netlify eligible + spam submissions checked / count removed:
Gmail + sent + accessible Trash + known local copies checked:
Historical Web3Forms: absent / controls used / request pending / follow-up:
Exports + recoverable copies checked / count removed:
Scoped exceptions: category / reason / due date or next review:
Provider action confirmed or pending / follow-up date:
```

**Owner approval recorded:** this routine and the privacy notice were approved on 20 November 2026. Perform the first review before public launch. Where historical provider deletion is still pending, retain the accurate qualification rather than claiming completion. This housekeeping action is separate from technical readiness for a private preview. See [ICO storage limitation](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/data-protection-principles/a-guide-to-the-data-protection-principles/storage-limitation/) and [launch control](human-hull-launch-control.md).
